consensus_summary: Consensus identifies the highway primarily as Isaiah’s prepared ‘Highway of Holiness’ (esp. 35:8) and ‘way of the Lord’ (40:3), the sanctified route of salvation by which God comes and the redeemed return home to Zion, applied christologically to John the Baptist’s preparatory ministry.
book_summary: The way of holiness — the prepared road home.
consensus_core_identification: prepared Highway of Holiness for God’s coming and the redeemed’s return/salvation
book_core_identification: the way of holiness as the prepared road home
rationale: Both cores name the identical Isaianic referent (Highway/Way of Holiness as the prepared route of return/salvation). The book’s terse phrasing ‘prepared road home’ simply restates the consensus’s dominant return-to-Zion motif without narrowing, broadening, or replacing it; extra consensus layers (John the Baptist, Gentile inclusion, moral application) are complementary expansions, not competing cores.
strongest_objection: The book omits explicit NT linkage to John the Baptist that every consensus response treats as central, yet this is an omitted extension rather than a contradictory core.
